part.candidateMoves.title: Candidate moves
part.candidateMoves.summary: Before calculating, list the checks, captures and threats; in quiet positions, the right move may be off the list.
ex.cm.XADiA: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.cm.XADiA.hint: The bishop on g5 and the queen on g6 aim at the black king. Calculate the captures with check.
ex.cm.XADiA.solution: 23.Bxf6+! The bishop captures the knight with check. After 23...Rxf6, 24.Qxf6+ captures the rook with check, and White wins material.
ex.cm.Dln0c: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.cm.Dln0c.hint: The rook on h1 is on the same file as the black king. Which bishop move takes advantage of that?
ex.cm.Dln0c.solution: 19.Bxd6+! The bishop captures the pawn on d6, uncovers the check from the rook on h1 and attacks the queen on e7. After 19...Kg8, 20.Bxe7 captures the queen.
ex.cm.LsN7f: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.cm.LsN7f.hint: The knight on d4 stands between your rook on d5 and the white queen. Look for its check.
ex.cm.LsN7f.solution: 19...Ne2+! The knight gives check and uncovers the attack of the rook on d5 on the queen on d1. If 20.Qxe2, 20...Qxe2 captures the queen; if the king steps out of check, 20...Rxd1 captures the queen.
ex.cm.i51Hs: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.cm.i51Hs.hint: The queen on d8 has only one defender. List the checks, even the ones that give up material.
ex.cm.i51Hs.solution: 26.Bg7+! The bishop gives check, defended by the queen, and the rook on g8 has to capture it. Without the rook on g8, the queen on d8 is undefended: 27.Qxd8+ captures it with check.
ex.cm.VbrcI: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.cm.VbrcI.hint: List the knight checks and calculate two moves. The pawn on g7 is pinned.
ex.cm.VbrcI.solution: 17.Nf7+! The knight gives check, and the king only has g8. After 17...Kg8, 18.Nh6+ is a fork: check to the king and an attack on the queen on f5. The pawn on g7 cannot take the knight, because it is pinned by the queen on g6.
ex.cm.YdtlM: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.cm.YdtlM.hint: The rook on d5 stands on the diagonal between the queen on b3 and the black king.
ex.cm.YdtlM.solution: 20.Rf5+! The rook leaves d5 with a discovered check from the queen on b3 and attacks the queen on f6. After 20...Kh8, 21.Rxf6 captures the queen.
ex.cm.iw2ZR: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.cm.iw2ZR.hint: Without the pawn on g2, the white king is exposed to your queen and the bishop on d6.
ex.cm.iw2ZR.solution: 29...Nxh3+! The knight captures the pawn on h3 with check. After 30.gxh3, 30...Qxh3 leaves the white king without the pawn on g2, and the queen and the bishop on d6 threaten mate on h2.
ex.cm.tVsT2: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.cm.tVsT2.hint: List the checks of the knight on h5. The pawn on g7 is pinned by the queen on g6.
ex.cm.tVsT2.solution: 26.Nf6+! The knight gives check and attacks the queen on g4, and the pawn on g7, pinned by the queen on g6, cannot take it. After 26...Rxf6, 27.Qxg4 fxg4 28.exf6, and White wins the rook for the knight.
ex.cm.yXcu5: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.cm.yXcu5.hint: List the checks, even the ones that give up the queen, and calculate the fork that follows.
ex.cm.yXcu5.solution: 21...Qxg2+! The queen captures the bishop on g2 and draws the king. After 22.Kxg2, 22...Nxe3+ is a fork: check to the king and an attack on the queen on d1. The rook on f3 cannot take the knight, because it is pinned by the bishop on b7. After 23.Kg1, 23...Nxd1 captures the queen.
